title: CRLR/151/2012 of PURAN SINGH CHAUHAN Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No.151 of 2012
Puran Singh Chauhan .....Revisionist
 (In Jail)

Versus
State of Uttarakhand ....Respondents
Present: Mr. S.K. Mandal, Advocate for the revisionist.
 Mr. Siddhartha Bisht, Brief Holder for the State of Uttarakhand.
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J. (Oral)
 The revisionist has been convicted by the court of Judicial
Magistrate, Ist Class Srinagar, Pauri Garhwal vide his judgment dated
20.05.2005 as rendered in Criminal Case No.448 of 2004, State vs. Puran
Singh Chauhan arising out of Case Crime No.06 of 1999, which was
registered by the complainant at Thana Srinagar, District Pauri Garhwal
alleging it to be for the offences complained of under Sections 379, 409,
420, 467, 468, 411 and 471 of IPC, which was registered at the aforesaid
police station. The judgment of conviction as rendered by the learned trial
court of Judicial Magistrate 1st Class which was imposed upon the
revisionist to the following effect:-
(1) For the offence under Section 420 IPC, the revisionist
has been directed to undergo a rigorous imprisonment of one
year and a fine of Rs.1,000/- has been imposed upon him and
in an event of failure to deposit the penalty, he had been

- 2 -
directed to further undergo one month of additional simple
imprisonment.
(2) For the offence under Section 467 IPC, the revisionist
has been imposed with a sentence of three years of rigorous
imprisonment and a penalty of Rs.2,000/- has been imposed
and in an event of failure to deposit the penalty, he had been
further directed to undergo two month of additional simple
imprisonment.
(3) For the offence under Section 468 IPC, revisionist has
been sentenced to undergo one year of rigorous imprisonment
and a fine of Rs.1,000/- has been imposed and in an event of
failure to deposit the penalty, he had been sentenced to
undergo further one month of simple imprisonment and;
(4) For the offence under Section 471 IPC he has been
sentenced to undergo one year of rigorous imprisonment and a
fine of Rs.1,000/- has been imposed and similarly in an event
of failure to deposit the penalty, he had been directed to
undergo a further sentence of one month of simple
imprisonment.

For the offences under Sections 379, 411 and 409 of IPC the
revisionist was acquitted of the charges by the court of Judicial Magistrate
1st Class, Srinagar, Pauri Garhwal vide his impugned judgment dated
20.05.2005.

- 3 -
2. The revisionist feeling himself to be aggrieved against the
judgment of conviction dated 20.05.2005, as rendered in the Criminal Case
No.448 of 2004, State vs. Puran Singh Chauhan had preferred a Criminal
Appeal by invoking the provisions contained under Section 374 of the
Cr.P.C. before the court of District and Sessions Judge, Pauri Garhwal,
which was registered as Criminal Appeal No.14 of 2005, Puran Singh
Chauhan vs. State of Uttarakhand. The appellate court, vide its impugned
judgment dated 06.08.2012 had partly allowed the Criminal Appeal and had
modified the sentence of conviction as imposed by the trial court to the
following effect:-
(a) The sentence of one year of rigorous imprisonment for
the offence under Section 420, 468 and 471 IPC, the fine of
Rs.1,000/- and also the additional sentence in the event of
failure to deposit the penalty for each of the aforesaid offences
has been affirmed and maintained by the appellate court;
(b) The sentence for the offence under Section 467 IPC as
imposed by the trial court was modified and consequently
sentencing the revisionist to undergo a sentence of one and
half years of rigorous imprisonment and a penalty of
Rs.2,000/- has been maintained and in an event of failure to
deposit the penalty within the time specified, the appellate
court has further directed the revisionist to undergo an
additional simple imprisonment for a period of two months.
3. As per the judgments under challenge both the sentences were
directed to run concurrently and it was further directed that the amount of

- 4 -
Rs.97,000/- which was recovered from the revisionist and deposited in the
State Treasury, the same will remain deposited with the State.
4. The prosecution story in short is that the complaint of the said
complainant, which was registered as Case Crime No.06 of 1999 by Mr.
Arvind Kumar, who at the relevant point of time, was working as an
Executive Engineer with the U.P. Jal Vidhyut Nigam Limited Camp,
Srinagar, Pauri Garhwal, he has said to have registered a complaint by way
of First Information Report (which is Ex.Ka.1) before P.S. Srinagar,
District Pauri Garhwal as back as on 04.01.1999. The set of allegations as
mentioned in the FIR No.6 of 1999, it was to the effect that the department
was having a Saving Bank Account, standing in the name of department
being Saving Bank Account No.13965 which is in the Punjab National
Bank, Branch Srinagar. It was alleged that as against the Account standing
in the name of department, a cheque book has been issued in favour of the
department and it was found, on inspection, being conducted by one of the
employees of the department Vimal Kant Chaturvedi on 04.01.1999 to the
effect that the cheque book, which has been issued thus by the Bank, as
against the said amount, one of the cheque's leaflet was found missing. It
was contended in the complaint that when the said register was checked by
the said Vimal Kant Chaturvedi, he found that the cheque, which was
missing, was not registered in the cheque book register in order to make the
relevant entries and also on comparing of the entries endorsed in the
register with regard to the cheque issued by the department, as against the
said Saving Bank Account then it has revealed that one cheque bearing
Cheque No.RTH389242 was found missing, and after getting the said

- 5 -
information about the missing cheque, the same was informed by Mr.
Vimal Kant Chaturvedi to the Project Director i.e. Executive Engineer Sri
Suresh Chandra Baluni and he alongwith other officials of the U.P. Jal
Vidhyut Nigam had went to the Branch of Punjab National and had
contacted the Branch Manager and after a meeting being held with him, the
bank had imparted the information from where it was revealed that the said
missing cheque bearing Cheque No.RTH389242 was drawn for an amount
of Rs.1,62,000/- and it is further shown that the said cheque for the
aforesaid amount is said to have been deposited in the Saving Bank
Account of the revisionist himself bearing Account No.11972. It was
further reflected from the information retrieving from Bank that after the
said deposit having been made by the revisionist into the bank account, it is
said that on the date of deposit of the cheque itself, out of the total deposit
of Rs.1,62,000/- a sum was shown to have been withdrawn by the
revisionist himself to the tune of Rs.1,60,000/-.
5. However, the controversy pertains to as to whether the deposit,
which has been made into the Saving Bank Account of the revisionist,
which was standing in the name of the Punjab National Bank, the said
deposit is being shown to have been made by Mr. Bharat Singh and the said
receipt finds place on record as Paper No.16 Ka. Later on, during the course
of investigation, it was reveled that as far as the withdrawal made by the
present revisionist, he had been alleged to have manipulated the documents
in order to get the benefit of the deposit made of the cheque in his account
on 04.01.1999 and the said manipulation he has been able to on account of
the fact that he has engaged on contractual basis in the U.P. Jal Vidhyut

- 6 -
Nigam Department at Srikot, Srinagar in the capacity of being a contract
Chaukidar. It is alleged by the prosecution that particularly, the FIR which
was registered by the Executive Engineer that the cheque which was said to
have been deposited into the account of the revisionist, the said cheque was
never endorsed by the officials of the Accounts Department of U.P. Jal
Vidhyut Nigam nor the same has been endorsed by the competent
authorities. It was contended by the department authorities that when the
revisionist was interrogated, during the course of interrogation he has
admitted his guilt by giving in writing and he has informed that now as of
after the withdrawal made of Rs.1,60,000/- only Rs.7,000/- is said to have
been left. It was further observed by the prosecution that the Project
Director Mr. Suresh Chandra Baluni and the Project Engineer Mr. N.P.
Singh, who had appeared before the departmental inquiry, they have
requested that on account of the manipulation being made for the purposes
of withdrawal of the said amount from the account of the department, a
criminal proceeding ought to have been initiated because of the admission
of the guilt by the revisionist before the competent authorities of having
indulged in wrongful withdrawal of the cheque and its ultimate deposit in
his account.
6. Based on the aforesaid set of allegation, it is contended by the
prosecution that the first information report Exh.Ka.1 was registered and as
per the G.D. Exh.Ka.42 it was found that the sum of Rs.7,000/- has been
deposited by the revisionist by way of Exh.Ka.2 and thereafter the
prosecution has proceeded and after conducting the inspection on the spot
that is a place from where the cheque was stolen, the site inspection report

- 7 -
was prepared as Exh.Ka.43, the accused persons were arrested as would be
apparent from the arrest memo by Exh.Ka.3 and thereafter from their
possession a sum of Rs.90,000/- was recovered for which the fard
baramadgi was prepared as Exh.Ka.4. As a consequence thereto, the
Investigating Officer had submitted the charge sheet in relation to the
commission of offence under Sections 379, 409, 420, 467, 468, 411 and
471 IPC, which finds place in the records of the lower court as Exh.Ka.54.
Ultimately, the revisionist was summoned, the trial commenced, a charge
was framed against him for commission of offences as aforesaid.
7. The prosecution in support of the contention that the cheque
thus stolen from the cheque book of the department was deposited into the
account of the revisionist and he was beneficiary of the deposit because he
has later on withdraw the said amount, the said story as narrated in the FIR
and ultimately established in the investigation was supported by the
prosecution witnesses i.e. PW.1 the Executive Engineer of the Uttar
Pradesh Jal Vidhyut Nigam, Uttarkashi, the Project Directors and the
Account Officers, who appeared as PW2 and PW3 respectively. In the
statements as recorded by PW4 Bharat Singh Rawat, who is later on shown
to have become hostile, is the person, who is as per the evidence on record
shown to have deposited the amount as would be apparent from Exh.Ka.16
as he was the person responsible for depositing the amount thus, withdrawn
by the cheque into account of the revisionist. Apart from that the
prosecution has led other oral testimonies of the other witnesses also who
were cross-examined and ultimately the revisionist too has recorded his
statement under Section 313 of Cr.P.C. though, he has made an effort to

- 8 -
deny the offence in his defence taken before the court below but this Court
cannot be oblivious of the fact at the time when the interrogation was made
by the departmental authorities, he in his writing has admitted the fact of
having involved in the commission of offence as alleged in the FIR.
8. Based on the aforesaid prosecution, the learned trial court
commenced the trial and thereafter on appreciation of evidence on record
and in particular, the statement recorded or the prosecution witness i.e.
PW.1 the complainant and also other supporting evidence i.e. G.D. report
i.e. Exh.39, it is contended that they have received an information through
telephone to the effect that the present revisionist, who was working as a
Chaukidar in the department, he was residing in a room, which was situated
at Rishikesh, Dehradun and he was awaiting there for the commission of
the said offence of encashment of the amount, which was wrongfully
withdrawn from the account of the Department. Learned trial court has also
considered the statement of PW4 recorded i.e. Bharat Singh Rawat to the
effect that he in his cross examination, which was recorded on 29.12.1998
has submitted that he has given a cheque to be deposited into the accounts
and the said cheque, which finds place as Exh.Ka.7 was deposited in his
account though he has expressed that he is not very sure that at the time
when the said cheque was being deposited into the account of the
revisionist whether he was present on the said place or not. But in nutshell
on appreciation of the evidence, it was proved beyond doubt;
(1) That the cheuqe was stolen.
(2) That the amount of the cheque i.e. Rs.1,60,000/- was
deposited

- 9 -
 into the accounts of the revisionist.
(3) On the same day an amount of Rs.1,60,000/- was
withdrawn.
 That in itself will lead to an inference that there was a nexus of
indulgment of the revisionist in commission of the said offence of taking
the benefit of the cheque, which was stolen and ultimately deposited in his
account. However, the learned trial court on culmination of the trial by the
judgment dated 20.05.2005 has convicted the revisionist for the offences
under Section 467 and 420 IPC and as a consequence thereto, for the
offence under Section 467 IPC he has been directed to undergo three years
of rigorous imprisonment and a penalty of Rs.2,000/- has been imposed and
in the event of failure he has been directed to further undergo simple
imprisonment for a period of two month. For the offence under Section 420
IPC he was directed to undergo sentence of one year and penalty of
Rs.1,000/- has been imposed and in the event of failure he has been directed
to undergo further sentence of one month simple imprisonment. As far as
the offence under Section 468 IPC is concerned he has been directed to
undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of one year and penalty of
Rs.1,000/- has been imposed on him and in the event of failure he has been
directed to undergo further one month's simple imprisonment. Similarly for
the offence under Section 471 IPC he has been directed to undergo sentence
of one year rigorous imprisonment and penalty of Rs.1,000/-has been
imposed upon him and in the event of failure he has been directed to further
undergo one month's simple imprisonment. On the contrary for the offence
under Section 379, 411 and 409 IPC he has been acquitted.

- 10 -
9. Being aggrieved against the judgment of acquittal rendered by
the court of Judicial Magistrate, Ist Class, Srinagar, Pauri Garhwal, the
revisionist has preferred a Criminal Appeal being Criminal Appeal No.14
of 2005, Pooran Singh Chauhan vs. State of Uttarakhand and the appellate
court has by the judgment under challenge before this Court, had reduced
the sentence as imposed by the learned trial court and as a consequence
thereto, for the offences under Section 420, 468 and 471 IPC he was
sentenced to undergo a rigorous imprisonment for a period of one year and
a penalty of Rs.1,000/- as imposed by the trial court was maintained as it
was. The sentence as imposed for the offence under Section 467 IPC by the
trial court to be of three years that has been reduced to one and a half year
of rigorous imprisonment, however, the penalty thereto of Rs.2,000/- has
been directed to be maintained.
10. What is important to be considered while scrutinizing the
appellate court's judgment is that though learned counsel for the revisionist
has addressed this Court on merits of the matter as to the manner in which
the prosecution has substantiated itself in commission of the offence, which
has been leveled against the revisionist, he has submitted that he cannot be
attributed for commission of an offence under Sections 467, 468 and 471
IPC, once he has been acquitted of the commission of an offence under
Section 379 and 411 IPC. He further submits that once the fact of stealing
of the cheque was not proved then simultaneously, he could not have been
punished for the offences under Sections 467, 468 and 471 IPC. Though
apparently it seems to be a very laudable argument to be considered while
this Court at the time of considering the present revision against the

- 11 -
judgment of conviction rendered by both the courts below. But what is to
be visualized also as pointed out by the counsel for the Government
Advocate to the effect that the contention, which was raised by the
revisionist that he was not aware of the fact as to who has deposited the
amount into his account is belied from the evidence on record because it
was PW4 who had appeared and recorded his statement before the court
below that he was the person, who has deposited amount as mentioned in
the cheque into account of the present revisionist but be that as it may.
What is important is that in para 7 of the appellate court's judgment though
the revisionist might have addressed sought to address the appellant court
on number of accounts on merits of the judgment of conviction but what is
recorded therein is that the revisionist has confined himself to argue at a
later stage on the sentence only and the following observations has been
made by the learned appellate court in para 7, which is quoted hereunder:-
" vfHk;qDr ds fo)ku vf/koDrk us esjs le{k cgl djrs gq, ;g rdZ j[kk x;k fd mUgsa

11. The learned counsel for the revisionist submits that the finding
as recorded in para 7 limiting the address on appeal on the quantum of
sentence, is the version, which has been extended by the counsel, who was
conducting the appeal and it was not the statement which was recorded by
the revisionist before the court below. He further submitted that such type
of statement is normally made by the Advocates conducting the
proceedings as against the judgment of conviction and hence it cannot be

- 12 -
said that said statement as recorded in para 7 for addressing the appellant
court confining his arguments on the sentence cannot be treated as to be the
statement recorded at the behest of the convict/revisionist. This Court is not
in agreement with the arguments extended by the learned counsel for the
revisionist from the said prospective for the reason being that first of all it is
a specific finding which has been recorded by the appellate court whereby
the revisionist has confined his argument to the sentence only; secondly if
the contention as raised by the counsel for the revisionist to the extent that
it was merely statement made by the counsel that is taken into consideration
as to have been made without his consent that cannot be accepted for the
reason being that the said ground has not been taken as a ground in the
revision for challenging the said finding recorded in para 7 of the judgment.
If that be the situation, where the revisionist himself has limited his
argument on the sentence only before the appellate court, in that eventuality
he has acquiesced his right to challenge the judgment of conviction on the
merits of its matter and the revisionist would only be confined with regards
to the sentence imposed by the appellate court, which has resulted into a
reduction of sentence for the offence under Section 467 IPC from three
years to one and half year of rigorous imprisonment though the penalty as
imposed by the trial court in relation to all other offences ,which was
proved against him was directed to be maintained including their respective
sentences of one year of rigorous imprisonment.
12. The counsel has further submitted that in the given set of
circumstances, since the finding recorded concurrently by both the courts
below does not reflected that there is any criminal antecedents as against

- 13 -
the present revisionist, hence he would be entitled for the benefit of the
provisions contained under Section 4 of the Probation of Offenders Act,
1958. This Court after having gone through the provisions contained under
Section 4 though it contemplates granting the benefit of the said provision
to the person convicted the commission of an offence which is not
punishable for a period of beyond death or life imprisonment but once he
has been found apparently to be guilty for commission of an offence by
both the courts below, it may not invariably attract the provisions of
Sections 4 attracted to be made applicable more particularly when there is
established offence by both the courts below with regards to the
commission of an offence under Sections 467, 468 and 471 IPC where the
public money is said to have been seconded and deposited into the account
of the revisionist which was later on withdrawn by him. Hence, This Court
is not inclined to extend the benefit of Section 4 of Probation of Offenders
Act, 1958.
13. In the memorandum of revision before this Court if that is
scrutinized in its decision, there is no such ground taken by the revisionist
to the effect that he has never recorded any statement confining his
argument before the appellate court from the view point of argument only
limited to the sentence. Meaning thereby once the said ground has not been
taken in the memorandum of revision as against the judgment of conviction
before this Court it would not be deemed that before the appellate court he
has confined his argument on the sentence only. Now comes to the question
of consideration of the modified sentence as imposed by the appellate court.
Yet again, if the grounds are taken into consideration as raised by the

- 14 -
revisionist and also argued before the court below, it was with regards to
that a conviction as made against the revisionist was contrary to the
provisions of law and the conviction order cannot be sustained because in
an eventuality where the theory of stealing the cheque is not proved against
him he could not have been convicted for the offences under Sections 467,
468 and 471 IPC. Stealing of cheque from the cheque book of the
department might not have been directly proved against him and hence, the
acquittal in relation thereto by the learned trial court would not leave to an
inference that he was not beneficiary of the deposit having being made into
his account of the cheque out of which he himself shown to have withdrawn
the amount as mentioned in the impugned judgment. Further more if the
finding recorded by the trial court is taken into consideration as far as the
commission of offence is concerned chastely there is an admission on
behalf of the revisionist before the court below that he has prayed for his
forgiveness for having indulged in the commission of offence as
complained of as against him.
14. In that eventuality since the appellate court has already taken a
considering view of reducing the sentence of the revisionist of his
conviction under Section 467 IPC from three years of rigorous
imprisonment to the period of one and half years of rigorous imprisonment
though maintaining the penalty as imposed for the aforesaid offences, this
Court is of the view that as soon as the revisionist has confined his
argument to the sentence and the revisional court has accordingly
considering the argument and the evidence which was relied by the
revisionist to be considered from that prospective of reducing the sentence,

- 15 -
hence the appellate court has already reduced the sentence as imposed by
the trial court. Consequently the finding which has been recorded by the
appellate court by virtue of which he has determined the aspects pertaining
to the so called mis-utilization of the public money of the department by the
wrongful withdrawal of the same and depositing in the account of the
revisionist and hence, the sentence imposed against the revisionist as
modified by the appellant by the judgment dated 06.08.2012 do not suffer
from any apparent error which cause for any interference in the exercise of
revisional jurisdiction. Consequently, this Court is not inclined to interfere
in the revision, the same is accordingly, dismissed. However, since the
revisionist was enlarged on bail by the order dated 17.08.2012 he is
directed to forthwith surrender before the Magistrate concerned to serve the
remaining sentence and the sureties as furnished by him for availing the
bail that stands discharge.
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 20.11.2019
